parsed.why: The national document, entry-screening and custody risks remain. Statewide protections and remedies, plus no enacted adult facility or presentation ban, modestly improve the local picture; the city sanctuary adds limited visitor protection.

The state adds enforced birth-sex facility and prison-placement rules and criminal penalties for gender-expression performance. These are serious visitor-facing exposures atop the restrictive national framework; the reported killing figure is an undercount floor, not a usable rate.

Birth-sex facility restrictions across public buildings, criminal and civil penalties, private bounty suits and invalidated state IDs create direct, recurring exposure for visitors, materially worsening the already restrictive national baseline.

The national risks remain, but this state adds no adult facility ban or criminalisation. Discrimination protections are uneven and hate-crime coverage lacks gender identity; youth restrictions and a pending care rule have limited direct bearing on adult visitors.

The national framework dominates. The state’s facility restriction applies to students in public schools and higher education, not visitors generally; prison-treatment limits are resident-facing. No additional general visitor exposure is documented.
